title: 55th Pacific Islands Forum Opens in Palau — Taiwan Attends Opening Ceremony in Unusually Visible Role
detail: The 55th Pacific Islands Forum Leaders Meeting opened in Palau on August 31, 2026 (running through September 4), with Taiwan Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung and a large Taiwanese business delegation attending the opening ceremony. Taiwan has participated as a forum "development partner" since 1993, and Palau — one of only three Pacific nations with formal diplomatic ties to Taipei, alongside the Marshall Islands and Tuvalu — gave Taiwan an unusually visible presence this year, including sideline events and direct engagement with member states such as Australia, the US and Japan. Analysts noted the contrast with the prior year's forum in the Solomon Islands (a China ally), where non-member states were blocked from attending entirely, excluding both Taiwan and China. Five of the forum's 18 members — Kiribati, Fiji, Vanuatu, Samoa and Solomon Islands — were absent from this year's gathering; New Zealand Foreign Minister Winston Peters called the collective absence "highly suspicious" without making a direct accusation.
